headline: The pipeline runs end to end on project-b for the first time (two prior attempts produced zero candidates ever). But the compile gate is a no-op on this project: a candidate with two deliberate type errors SURVIVED with score 1.00. No survival rate is reported, because the contract that defines 'survived' is not being enforced here.

project.existing_test: src/utils/tests/array.test.ts — the module HAS gained a test since the brief was written
project.ts_jest_diagnostics: the project sets diagnostics:false itself, so ADR-0036 fix 1 was never needed here

doctor.stryker_runner: ok — jest, . can be mutated under that runner

a_stryker_loads_plugins.evidence: generated sidecrew.stryker.config.mjs carries absolute plugins paths into node_modules/.pnpm/ for BOTH @stryker-mutator/jest-runner and @stryker-mutator/typescript-checker, with the default glob '@stryker-mutator/*' kept first. Stryker ran to completion: 6 mutants, 6 killed, score 1.00. Neither 'Unknown stryker config option "jest"' nor 'Cannot find Checker plugin "typescript"' occurred.
a_stryker_loads_plugins.note: ADR-0036 fix 2 was built against a six-file reproduction; this is its first real project.

b_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.evidence: A candidate whose first line is `import { describe, it, expect } from '@jest/globals'` SURVIVED: compile ok, pass ok, 6/6 mutants killed. @jest/globals is genuinely NOT a declared dependency and does NOT resolve via node's resolver from the project root, but jest's own resolver supplies it at runtime.
b_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.caveat: The TS2307 that would otherwise have fired is suppressed by prediction (c) — tsc never type-checks the candidate. So (b) is refuted in observable effect, but one of the two mechanisms that would have caught it is itself broken.

c_tsc_does_not_check_the_candidate.verdict: CONFIRMED — and it is a hole in the gate
c_tsc_does_not_check_the_candidate.mechanism: testDirFor returns 'test', a directory that does not exist in this project (its tests live in src/utils/tests/). tsconfig.json has include: ["src", "internals/startingTemplate/**/*", "src/types/**/*"]. The candidate is written to test/<name>.test.ts, outside every include glob, so `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` type-checks the project and not the candidate.

control_1.result: compile ok — failed only at the pass stage, as a runtime ReferenceError

control_2.candidate: const wrongType: string = 42 (module scope) and const alsoWrong: number = 'not a number' (inside the test) — both type errors, neither throws at runtime
control_2.result: SURVIVED · compile ok · pass ok · 6 mutants killed · score 1.00

c_tsc_does_not_check_the_candidate.consequence: On this project the 'compiles' conjunct of `survive <=> compiles AND passes AND kills >= 1 AND non-tautological` is not enforced. A survivor can reach Claude's review having never been type-checked, and would fail the project's own CI tsc step.

d_tsc_ooms_without_more_heap.verdict: CONFIRMED, and better handled than predicted
d_tsc_ooms_without_more_heap.evidence: Without NODE_OPTIONS, tsc --noEmit ran out of memory after 48.9 s (predicted ~52 s).
d_tsc_ooms_without_more_heap.handling: sidecrew did NOT report it as a failed candidate. It refused with a distinct error naming the cause as a machine limit rather than the candidate, and printing the exact remedy plus the fact that it passes the environment through.
d_tsc_ooms_without_more_heap.deviation_recorded: NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 was set for every subsequent verify. This is an environment change, not a verifier change.
d_tsc_ooms_without_more_heap.doctor_gap: doctor still cannot see this coming — it reports tsc ok without knowing the heap the project needs.

new_defect_found.title: ADR-0036's two fixes do not compose: fix 1 is silently disabled on exactly the package manager fix 2 exists to support
new_defect_found.mechanism: src/verifier/ts.ts:776 gates the jest shim on `runner === "jest" && isResolvable("ts-jest", projectDir) && isResolvable("jest-config", projectDir)`. Under pnpm's strict layout jest-config is a transitive dependency of jest and is NOT resolvable from the project root, so the shim is skipped. Measured here: ts-jest resolves, jest-config does not.
new_defect_found.impact_here: None — project-b sets ts-jest diagnostics:false in its own config, so it never needed the shim.
new_defect_found.impact_elsewhere: A pnpm project on ts-jest with diagnostics left at the default would get no remedy and no explanation, and would fail exactly as ADR-0028 describes. Fix 2 makes pnpm reach the mutation stage; fix 1 then cannot help it when it gets there.
new_defect_found.not_fixed: No verifier code was touched during this trial.

mutant_probe.significance: The first measurement of any kind this project has produced. ADR-0030's trial and the one before it never got a single candidate to a verdict.

survival_rate_withheld_because: Prediction (c) shows the compile stage does not type-check the candidate on this project. Any survival rate measured here would be over a weaker contract than sidecrew's stated one, and not comparable with project-a's 0.375. Fix the gate, then measure.
